originalCard.questionText:
Write a summary in English of the content of each Section as instructed.

Section 1
How did the writer end up spending two years in two English boarding schools? Give five details.

Section 2
Anna describes how the British educational system differs from the Russian one. Give five details.

Section 3
Apart from classroom learning, what activities do British boarding schools support? Give five details.

Section 4
What benefits has Anna derived from studying in British schools? Give five details.

rubric.markingGuideNote: The original paper gives 40 marks for summary writing; the final marking scheme gives 45 for the complete section. This joint task retains all four original questions and the final scheme’s collective maximum, without assigning a fixed 11/12 split to individual sections. Assess each section’s content manually against its complete published pool and five-distinct-details rule, including Section 2’s all-four-category requirement and two-mark subject-list maximum, and Section 3’s two-boy-sport limit and one-mark leisure details up to four. The numerical controls record your manual assessment; they do not count or classify individual details. Normal discretion is one, or two for a particularly well-answered question. If the response fails to answer all required sections/subsections, select the printed condition to withhold all discretionary marks. Assess language manually for each section. Read the general no-marks instruction alongside the summary-specific discretion exception. The scheme gives no numerical or wholly/mixed-language threshold; do not automatically remove discretionary marks merely because Russian words appear. English or Irish is permitted by the original bilingual paper.
